title: Establish upgrade compatibility matrix and pinning strategy for Terraform modules/providers for Private VPC
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) customers run their infra with a combination of Redwood Terraform modules (redwood/private-vpc, redwood/db, redwood/networking) and cloud providers (hashicorp/aws, hashicorp/azurerm, hashicorp/google). We currently lack a single canonical compatibility matrix mapping Redwood Private releases to tested Terraform module versions and provider constraints, which leads to upgrade surprises (provider API changes, module inputs renamed, drift).

Goal: Produce an upgrade compatibility matrix and a clear version pinning policy for Terraform modules and providers that we will publish in the private-deployments repo and Confluence, enforce via CI, and use as the source-of-truth for upgrades and customer runbooks. The matrix must cover: Redwood Private control-plane release, recommended module versions, provider versions/constraints, known breaking changes, and required tfengine/terraform version.

Scope: Only affects Private (VPC) deployment IaC maintained by Redwood. Includes testing and CI changes (plan-only gating), documentation, and an upgrade runbook. Does NOT include customer-managed forks except where we publish recommended pins for customers to consume.

Outcomes: 1) Compatibility matrix artifact in the repo; 2) Pinning policy committed to modules (module versions and provider constraints); 3) CI checks that fail if module/provider pins fall outside matrix; 4) Runbook for in-place upgrades with health-check checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix published as markdown at docs/terraform-compatibility.md in private-deployments repo and linked from Confluence
All active redwood/private-* modules have explicit module versions and provider constraints updated in main branch according to the matrix
CI pipeline includes a terraform plan job against the latest sandbox that validates provider/module versions and fails on drift
Upgrade runbook with step-by-step canary process, rollback commands, and health-check thresholds exists and is reviewed
At least one end-to-end upgrade test (control-plane 2026.02 -> 2026.03) executed in staging and results attached to ticket

notes:
Pinning strategy recommendation (draft):
- Modules: pin exact minor (e.g., v1.4.2) for control; allow patch updates via automated dependabot if tests pass.
- Providers: prefer constrained ranges that lock major and minor where we have verified compatibility (e.g., >= 4.12, < 5.0) or ~> 4.12 where provider uses semver semantics.
- Terraform CLI: standardize on 1.5.x for private releases; document required 'terraform' and 'terraform_binaries' in matrix.
Trade-offs: strict pinning reduces risk but increases the maintenance burden; we recommend conservative minor-level pins with an automated quarterly upgrade lane.
Safety: each provider/module upgrade must go through staging with plan+apply and automated health checks before inclusion in the matrix.
implementation_notes: Automation and CI details: create a 'compatibility-check' job that: 1) fetches matrix CSV from docs/, 2) compares current providers.lock and module versions, 3) fails fast and posts comment with diff. Use terraform 1.5.8 binary in CI image. Add a 'matrix/fixtures' folder with canonical providers.lock used for golden tests. Also add an e2e 'upgrade-sanity' workflow that runs against a short-lived sandbox org. Link PR: #286.
